intended_property: §6.1 Three-valued logic: a predicate evaluates to UNKNOWN on `NULL`, and the row enters neither side's result — not "NULL is false", and not "NULL is true" (M1a Phase 2 Task 3)
The type checks must not over-reject: `IS NOT NULL` is type-agnostic and must stay legal on TEXT columns

§6.3 `Arrangement::get` must return every value of a key (key → many values), not an `Option` — v0's group-by stores one value per key and has no use for more, but each side of a join is key → many rows, and the shape must hold now. Since M1b Phase 3a `get` returns `Result<Vec<(Row, i64)>, StateError>` rather than `Box<dyn Iterator<...>>` (every method can fail once a real shadow-table implementation exists), but the multi-value shape itself is unchanged
§5.1 A (key, val) whose weight reaches zero must be removed, leaving no zombie entry

§6.2 An aggregate must **retract the row it last emitted** — when SUM goes from 100 to 150 it emits `(key,100) w=-1` and `(key,150) w=+1`, not a single `+1` row. This is the real reason aggregation needs state: the operator must remember what it emitted in order to retract it (M1a Phase 2 Task 4). Since M1b Phase 1 what it remembers is the accumulators: the row to retract, `old_out`, is recomputed from the group's **old** stored state rather than kept as `g.emitted` (the plan's Ruling 1)
§6.1 With several aggs, `accs[i]` must correspond one-to-one with `aggs[i]`, not all share `accs[0]`

§6.2 `AggState` must survive across batches — only by keeping a batch's accumulators until the next batch can the next batch recompute, and so retract, the row the previous one emitted (before M1b Phase 1, `emitted` recorded "what was last emitted" and had to be kept for the same reason)

§5.2 `COUNT(*)` must equal the group's **total weight**, not its number of delta rows — a Z-set row can carry any weight, and a `rows += 1` implementation diverges as soon as weights differ from ±1 or a group has several rows (M1a Phase 2 Task 4)

§6.1 (measured) `SUM` must output `NULL` when "the group is non-empty but the column is entirely NULL", and SQLite outputs `NULL` too; an implementation that keeps only the running sum outputs `0`, and the disagreement is **silent** — so the state must keep both `sum` and `non_null` (M1a Phase 2 Task 4)

The counterpart to the previous row: `SUM`'s test must be "were there any non-NULL inputs", not "is the sum 0" — with non-NULL inputs that happen to sum to 0, it must output `Int(0)`, not `NULL` (M1a Phase 2 Task 4)
`SUM` must accumulate `v * w`, scaling each input by its weight, not ignore the weight with `+= v` (M1a Phase 2 Task 4)
§5.2 group key → exactly one output row, and outgoing delta weights are always ±1; a group's internal weight lives only in operator state and must not leak into the output (M1a Phase 2 Task 4)

§5.1 Once a group is completely empty, its state is removed — since M1b Phase 1, `AggState::store` stores nothing for a group whose `GroupState` is all zero (`is_empty`), so the group disappears from its arrangement, as it will from its `__ivm_state_<view>_<op>` table (before M1b Phase 1: once `rows == 0` and `emitted == None`, the group was removed from `groups`)

The same mutation as the previous row (`.take(1)`), pinning a different property — item 4 of the "join landing" checklist at the end (added in M1a Phase 2 Task 5, the **engine-side** counterpart of items 1-3): a non-anchor table's initial rows must actually be absorbed into the view by bootstrap, even when `initial` provides state for every table. This differs from the previous row: that one tests "does a missing state raise an error", this one "is a provided state actually used"
§8.5 `refresh` must drain `pending` (`std::mem::take`), not merely read it (`clone`) — otherwise the same batch of deltas is pushed through the operator tree again on the next `refresh`

**M1a Phase 2 Task 5 re-review Finding 2**: when `create_view` declares a table but cannot find its state in `initial`, it must fail rather than quietly treat it as empty — the differential harness's `gen_initial` always fills every table in `db.tables()`, so this path is structurally unreachable at the differential level, while M1b's hand-built `initial` (say, rebuilding a view for only some tables) will genuinely hit it. When `engine.rs` landed this branch had **zero `#[test]`s**, and its only explanatory comment claimed parity with the oracle side's `missing_base_state_for_a_declared_table_is_an_error` — that test is real, this one was not, so the comment misled readers into thinking it was guarded too

`IncrementalEngine::snapshot` (named `materialize` before re-review Finding 1; see the rename row below) must return the `view` accumulated so far, not a constant empty `ZSet` — it is the only way `IncrementalEngine` exposes its state

§6.2 The **engine-level** form of the above (the "node-level form" row above hands its debt here): `refresh` must reuse the `self.tree` built by `create_view`, not `Node::build` afresh from the plan every time — rebuilding makes `AggState` lose all its state between two refreshes, so every refresh starts from empty groups, never retracts what it last emitted, and emits only bare `+1`s (M1a Phase 2 Task 5)

§8.2 The same row value appearing in two tables must not be merged across tables — per-table merging is a correctness requirement, not just a performance one: merging across tables would let one table's changes silently cancel another's
